hero.title:
From my Mac 
to yours.
hero.lede: Native Mac apps for my daily driver: video library, updates, mail, backups. Built for me, shared with everyone. Open source.

apps.name: Renamy
apps.description: Renames and organizes your personal video library using official TMDB metadata. Preview every change before it happens.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: I used FileBot for years. When I went looking for a free, open-source alternative that fit the way I work, I couldn't find one. So I built my own, with speed and simplicity as the whole point.

items.title: Smart title detection
items.text: Finds the movie or show title in messy filenames by anchoring on the year or the season number.

items.title: Official metadata
items.text: Titles and years come from TMDB, so every file gets the same, correct name.

items.title: TV series
items.text: Understands `SxxExx` episodes and asks once for a whole season when a title is ambiguous.

items.title: Plex, Jellyfin & Emby
items.text: Optional folder structure and ID tags in the formats media servers expect.

items.title: Fix any match
items.text: Search by title, TMDB ID or a themoviedb.org link when the guess is wrong.

items.title: Undo
items.text: Revert the last rename or move, including the folders it created.

apps.name: PS2 Manager
apps.description: Organizes backups of the PS2 and PS1 games you own for Open PS2 Loader. Cover art, game IDs and file names, all sorted out for you.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: I'm a huge retrogamer. After too many late nights with outdated tools and wrong guides, I finally figured out how OPL actually expects things to be laid out. I wrote a few terminal scripts to prepare the hard drive or MX4SIO for my Free McBoot PS2, so I could play without putting my physical collection at risk. The GUI was the natural next step.

items.title: Drag & drop install
items.text: Drop PS2 `.iso` backups to copy them, PS1 `.cue`/`.bin` backups to convert them to `.VCD`.

items.title: PS1 via POPStarter
items.text: Creates the launcher for each game with your own imported files and copies the right patches.

items.title: Multi-disc games
items.text: Groups discs, writes the files OPL needs and renames everything to a standard format.

items.title: Titles & covers
items.text: Game names read from the disc image, covers downloaded one by one or for the whole library.

items.title: Per-game settings
items.text: Compatibility modes, virtual memory cards and cheats for every game.

items.title: Tools
items.text: Rename, export, convert back to BIN/CUE, defragment and delete, with a queue and progress.

apps.name: Tazzina
apps.tagline: The world needed one more caffeine app. Probably.
apps.description: A menu bar app with timed sessions, automatic triggers, sounds, and closed-lid mode. Brewed in Italy.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: I wanted something like Amphetamine, but simpler, lighter, and open source. There were already a thousand of them. This is number 1,001.

items.title: One click
items.text: Left click on the cup turns it on or off, right click opens the menu.

items.title: Sessions
items.text: Indefinitely, for a while, until a time, or as long as an app is running.

items.title: Triggers
items.text: Stays awake on its own when your rules match: apps, Wi-Fi, displays, power, battery, time, devices.

items.title: Closed lid
items.text: Keeps a MacBook running with the lid closed, and always restores normal sleep afterwards.

items.title: Safety
items.text: Ends the session when the battery is low or the charger is unplugged.

items.title: Automation
items.text: `tazzina://` links for Terminal and Shortcuts.

apps.name: Encody
apps.tagline: Power users still get the cockpit, just not by default.
apps.description: Re-encodes and remuxes your video library, keeping HDR10, HDR10+ and Dolby Vision intact. Drop, encode, done, or dive into every audio and subtitle track.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: After years of HandBrake, I realized I only ever used three or four presets of my own, refined over time for exactly what I needed. So I wrote a small terminal tool that ran just those, and called it MediaEnc. That tool became the engine behind Encody.

items.title: Batch queue
items.text: Drop files or folders, reorder, enable or skip items, import and export the queue.

items.title: HDR aware
items.text: Detects HDR10, HDR10+, HLG and Dolby Vision and re-injects the dynamic metadata after encoding.

items.title: Presets you can trust
items.text: Custom presets are saved only after a real test encode passes.

items.title: Film grain detection
items.text: Measures grain on every file and suggests the right preset.

items.title: Benchmark & quality check
items.text: Compare presets on automatic samples and check results with VMAF, XPSNR, ColorVideoVDP or SSIM.

items.title: Track selection
items.text: Choose audio and subtitle tracks per file, with smart audio modes.

notes.text: Every file gets its own settings

Pick how audio is handled:
**Pass** keeps it untouched

apps.name: Upgrady
apps.description: Checks every app on your Mac for updates, Homebrew casks included, and installs them for you.
apps.note: Fork of Latest by Max Langer

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: MacUpdater started giving me trouble on macOS 27. I'd tried Latest years earlier and loved it, but it was missing a few things I relied on. Updaty takes the best of both: exactly what I needed, nothing more.

items.title: Menu bar app
items.text: Lives in the menu bar with the number of available updates, and opens at login silently.

items.title: Homebrew integration
items.text: Apps installed with Homebrew are updated through `brew`, so it always stays in sync.

items.title: Third-party taps
items.text: Reads every installed tap, including personal ones like `gionnio/tap`.

items.title: Release notes
items.text: Shows the GitHub release notes of every version you are skipping.

items.title: Adopt manual installs
items.text: Links apps installed by hand to their Homebrew cask.

items.title: Background checks
items.text: Checks on a schedule and notifies you when updates are found.

apps.name: Posta
apps.description: A native Liquid Glass Gmail client: Apple Mail's feel with Gmail's labels, search and conversations.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: Come on, who doesn't want their Gmail account in Apple Mail, without all the usual limitations?

items.title: Mail-style layout
items.text: Mailboxes and nested labels, conversation list and full threads, like Apple Mail.

items.title: Real Gmail
items.text: Labels, threads, archive, stars and Gmail search syntax through the Gmail API.

items.title: Liquid Glass
items.text: A native toolbar with grouped actions that feels at home on macOS.

items.title: Notifications
items.text: Reply, archive or delete straight from the notification.

items.title: Always there
items.text: Keeps syncing from the menu bar when the window is closed.

items.title: Keyboard first
items.text: Mail shortcuts plus optional Gmail single-key shortcuts.
